overview.headline: How volcanoes create ash, lava, and mudflow hazards

keyPoints.point: Students learn that large explosive eruptions endanger people hundreds of miles away and affect global climate.
keyPoints.quote: Large explosive eruptions can endanger people and property hundreds of miles away and even affect global climate.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that volcanic ash in the cloud poses a serious hazard to aviation.
keyPoints.quote: The volcanic ash in the cloud can pose a serious hazard to aviation.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that carbon dioxide is heavier than air and can be trapped in low areas at deadly concentrations.
keyPoints.quote: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and can be trapped in low areas in concentrations that are deadly to people and animals.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that some lahars look like fast moving rivers of wet concrete because of rock debris.
keyPoints.quote: Some lahars contain so much rock debris (60 to 90% by weight) that they look like fast-moving rivers of wet concrete.

keyTerms.gloss: Solid and molten rock fragments blasted from explosive eruptions
keyTerms.quote: An explosive eruption blasts solid and molten rock fragments (tephra) and volcanic gases into the air with tremendous force.

keyTerms.gloss: Small openings in the ground where gases reach the surface
keyTerms.quote: Even when a volcano is not erupting, cracks in the ground allow gases to reach the surface through small openings called fumaroles.

keyTerms.gloss: Molten rock that pours onto the surface to form flows
keyTerms.quote: Molten rock (magma) that pours or oozes onto the Earth’s surface is called lava and forms lava flows.

keyTerms.gloss: Hot ash avalanches that move at high speeds down valleys
keyTerms.quote: These pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.

keyTerms.gloss: Flows of volcanic mud and debris on the flanks of a volcano
keyTerms.quote: Mudflows or debris flows composed mostly of volcanic materials on the flanks of a volcano are called lahars.

keyTerms.gloss: Irregular mounds formed when thick lava squeezes out of a vent
keyTerms.quote: Dacite and rhyolite lavas often squeeze out of a vent to form irregular mounds called lava domes.
